title: Maximum Equal Adjacent Pairs After at Most One Replacement
solution: Key observation: replacing every x with y never destroys an equal pair ((x,x) becomes (y,y)) and never creates one out of an (x,z) pair with z != y (it becomes (y,z), still unequal); the only new equal pairs are adjacent positions holding {x,y} in either order. So the answer is B + max over unordered value pairs {a,b}, a != b, of the number of adjacent positions i with {nums[i], nums[i+1]} = {a,b}, where B is the current count of equal adjacent pairs (the gain is 0 if no unequal adjacent pair exists, i.e. do nothing). Count unordered unequal adjacent pairs keyed by (min, max) in a hash map in one pass. O(n) time and space for n up to 1e5 with values up to 1e9.

solution_check.verified: true - gives 2, 4, 2 on the three examples, and matches a brute force over all (x,y) choices on 3000 random small arrays.

rejected_tags.reason: No greedy choice or exchange argument; taking the max of a frequency table is just an argmax, and the proposal's own notes admit greedy is filler.

notes.solver: Solution is an observation plus frequency counting of unordered adjacent pairs; no DP or greedy choice beyond picking the max-frequency pair. 'greedy' kept only as a broad tag (picking the best single pair), not as a pattern. Rejected brute-force over value pairs (O(distinct^2 * n) too slow) and any DP framing.
notes.skeptic: Independently derived the same O(n) solution: (x,x)->(y,y) stays equal, {x,y} adjacent becomes equal, (x,z) with z!=y stays unequal, so answer = existing equal pairs + max frequency of an unordered unequal adjacent pair (0 if none). Verified 2/4/2 on samples and against brute force over all (x,y) on 5000 random small arrays. Values up to 1e9 force hashing (or sort-based counting) rather than an array index. Summary lightly rewritten to state why only {x,y}-adjacent positions gain (original was accurate, 69 words, but omitted that half of the observation).
